vulnerability: Weak or easily guessed passwords can allow attackers to access user accounts.
recommended_control: Enforce appropriate password length and strength controls, and prevent commonly used passwords.
exact_parameter: Password length, password blocklist and password policy

vulnerability: Insecure password storage can expose user credentials if the database is compromised.
recommended_control: Store passwords using a secure adaptive hashing algorithm such as Argon2id, scrypt or PBKDF2.
exact_parameter: Password hashing algorithm, salt and work factor

vulnerability: Unsafe password-hash comparison can expose information through timing differences.
recommended_control: Use a secure password comparison function provided by the programming language or framework.

vulnerability: Automated attacks such as brute force and credential stuffing can compromise user accounts.
recommended_control: Apply login protections such as rate limiting, monitoring and multifactor authentication.
exact_parameter: Login attempt limits, rate limiting and MFA

vulnerability: An attacker with access to an active session may attempt sensitive account changes.
recommended_control: Require users to confirm their current credentials before sensitive account changes or transactions.
exact_parameter: Re-authentication for password, email and sensitive transaction changes

vulnerability: Without unique salts, identical passwords can produce matching hashes and make bulk cracking easier.
recommended_control: Generate a unique random salt for each password and include it in the password-hashing process.

vulnerability: An attacker who obtains password hashes from a database may attempt to crack them.
recommended_control: Consider using a pepper as an additional secret stored separately from the password database.
exact_parameter: Pepper secret and its secure storage location

vulnerability: Low password-hashing work factors can make password cracking faster.
recommended_control: Configure an appropriate work factor to make password hashing computationally expensive.
exact_parameter: Password hashing work factor or cost setting

vulnerability: Using an unsuitable password-hashing algorithm can weaken stored password protection.
recommended_control: Prefer Argon2id for password storage and configure its parameters according to security and performance needs.
exact_parameter: Argon2id memory, time and parallelism parameters

vulnerability: Using outdated or weak password-hashing settings can make password hashes easier to crack.
recommended_control: Use bcrypt mainly for legacy systems when Argon2 or scrypt is unavailable, with a work factor of at least 10.

vulnerability: Concatenating untrusted input into SQL statements can allow attackers to change query behavior.
recommended_control: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements to keep SQL structure separate from user-supplied values.
exact_parameter: SQL parameter binding and prepared statements

vulnerability: Untrusted input used for SQL identifiers or query structure can introduce injection risks.
recommended_control: Use an allow-list of permitted table names, column names or sort directions when these choices must be dynamic.
exact_parameter: Allow-listed SQL identifiers and permitted query options

vulnerability: Excessive database permissions can increase the damage caused by a successful SQL injection attack.
recommended_control: Give application database accounts only the permissions required for their tasks.

vulnerability: Manual escaping of untrusted SQL input is error-prone and can fail to prevent injection.
recommended_control: Avoid manually escaping SQL values. Use parameterized queries instead.
exact_parameter: SQL parameter binding instead of manual escaping

vulnerability: Invalid or unexpected input can create application security risks, including SQL injection when used unsafely.
recommended_control: Validate input according to expected type, length and format, while continuing to use parameter binding.
exact_parameter: Input type, length and format validation
